catalog_quote: There is no length contrast, but open-syllable vowels optionally lengthen under main stress. ... Apart from a few lexical exceptions, main stress is initial in the prosodic word. Secondary stress follows a trochaic rhythm of bimoraic feet (with closed syllables counting as heavy), but is blocked from final open syllables. Phonetically, unstressed open syllables can be reduced in non-final position, e.g. (ˈphagi)(ˌdet)(ˌlem) 'butterfly': [ˈphagɪˌdetˌlem] ~ [ˈphagˌdetˌlem]. The prosodic word starts at stem boundaries, e.g. ʔu(ˈhopchi) from u-hop-chi '3sgPOSS-calebash-nsg', unless this results in end stress, e.g. (ˈʔuhop). The prosodic word often fails to align with the morphological word, mostly because of the multifunctional prefix N- '3nsgS/A; 3A; NEG; 2sgPOSS', which is realized as a nasality feature on preceding codas ... sources.quote: 'Stress in these languages [Belhare and Limbu] follows a progressive trochaic pattern starting from the first stem mora. That the relevant feet are defined by bimoraicity, rather than bisyllabicity is evidenced by Belhare examples like labhokarik ... (φ 'labho)ka(φ ˌrik) ... Belhare bans degenerate feet ... The only exception to the ban on degenerate feet is monomoraic syllables under word-initial (i.e., main) stress: (φ 'mi) fire, or (φ 'sa)(ˌmet).' Also p.3: 'There is but one main stress (on the first stem-syllable)' in polysynthetic words.
sources.locator: ZORA PDF p.7 (printed footer 7), discussion of Belhare/Limbu feet

sources.quote: 'the Belhare stress pattern basically follows a trochaic rhythm of bimoraic feet (i.e., |σLσL or |σH). Feet are constructed in a left-to-right parse. ... On the word level, the End Rule starts from left and stress assignment is iterative. Secondary stress is therefore placed on every non-initial foot: ('noka)(ˌcik) brain, ('phek)(ˌkuli) buckwheat, ('sam)(ˌbhik) garlic ... foot structure is quantity-sensitive (pace Bickel 1996a, b) ... an additional rule of root-initial stress.
